verdict_reason: Titles match their assertions and each test can fail, but the multi-page species lookup has no test and the MockMvc set-up is copied from the sibling MDM controller tests.

todos.issue: No test reads a saved page after page 0. ProductController.getCommoditySpecies keeps one body per page and answers pages.get(page) (line 97-98), and the fixture saves two pages for 01061900 (100 + 20 species), which reference-data's SpeciesCheckService pages through. Every species test asks for page 0, an unknown code, or a page past the last one, so replacing 'pages.has(page)' with 'page == 0' leaves every test green.
todos.fix: Must: a test fails if the stub stops answering a saved page other than page 0. One way: getCommoditySpecies_shouldAnswerTheSavedSecondPage_forACodeWithTwoSavedPages, asking 01061900 page=1 size=100 and asserting content.length() == 20, page == 1 and totalElements == 120.

todos.issue: Test set-up copied a third time: the @WebMvcTest @Import list (LatencyConfig, StubLatencies, StubFaults, GlobalExceptionHandler, FileUtils) at lines 19-21, KEY_HEADER and ANY_KEY at lines 24-25, and the trace-header literals 'x-ms-middleware-request-id' / 'stub-trace-id' (lines 37, 89, 120) repeat CountriesControllerTest:24-30 and PortsOfEntryControllerTest:26. House rule: set-up used by two tests goes in the shared helper.
todos.fix: Must: the MDM controller tests share one home for the MockMvc slice imports, the subscription-key header and the expected trace header, and ProductControllerTest uses it instead of local copies. One way: a meta-annotation (e.g. @MdmStubWebMvcTest) carrying the @Import list, plus a small MdmStubTestRequests helper with the header constants, adopted by all three MDM controller tests.
